content:
# GitLab push approval (`code_request_push`)

## What to build

On GitLab, a push can start CI, and CI can read repository secrets. The product decision is that **every push to a GitLab repository needs the user's approval of the exact commit** (PRD user story 5b; section 9, push rule 4).

This slice adds a bot tool, `code_request_push({ repository, branch })`.
- Before the effect is recorded, the server reads the following from the bot's clone on its computer:
  - the local branch's commit SHA;
  - the commit subjects not yet on the remote;
  - a diff stat.
- It then shows an explicit approval card titled **"Push to GitLab?"**. The card has only Allow once and Deny; there is no "always".
- On approval, the handler stores a `GitPushApproval` row for `{ runId, botRepositoryId, ref, newSha, effectId }`.

The git proxy then requires every ref update in a GitLab push to match an unused approval from the same run, then marks it used. Any other GitLab push is refused with `rakazo: GitLab pushes need approval; call code_request_push first`, or `... the approved commit was <sha7>; call code_request_push again` when the SHA differs. GitHub pushes are not affected.

Already in the codebase:

- **`GitPushApproval` model:** `{ id, spaceId, userId, runId → Run, botRepositoryId → BotRepository, ref, newSha, effectId @unique, usedAt?, createdAt }`, with RLS.
- **`apps/api/src/git-proxy.ts` (receive-pack):**
  - parses commands into `PushCommand { oldSha, newSha, ref }` (helpers in `apps/api/src/git-pkt.ts`);
  - applies `checkPushCommands` and `checkFastForwards` from `apps/api/src/git-push-policy.ts`;
  - then runs `extraPushChecks?: Array<(ctx) => Promise<PushDecision>>` from its deps, where `PushDecision = { ok: true } | { ok: false; message; perRef }`;
  - refuses with `receivePackRefusal`, so git shows `remote: <message>` and `[remote rejected] (rakazo policy)`;
  - audits `code.push`.
- **`packages/adapters/src/code-repo-tools.ts`:**
  - `code_repos` and `code_repo_checkout`;
  - `CODE_REPO_TOOL_NAMES`;
  - `clonePath(provider, fullPath)` (`repos/<host>/<fullPath>`, resolved with `resolveBotWorkspacePath(ctx.computer.mode, bot.id, …)`);
  - an exec helper running argv on the computer via `ctx.deps.sandbox.execute`.
- **Tool selection:** `code-repo-tools-select.ts` drops `CODE_REPO_TOOL_NAMES` unless `codeReposEnabled`.
- **`packages/core/src/code-host-branch.ts`:** `isBotBranchRef(ref, prefix)`.
- **`BotRepository`:** has `branchPrefix`, `defaultBranch`, `fullPath` and `connection.provider`.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `packages/core/src/action-approval.ts`:
  - line 33: `APPROVAL_REQUIRED_BUILTIN_TOOLS`;
  - line 51: `EXPLICIT_APPROVAL_BUILTIN_TOOLS`, which is never auto-reviewed and has no "Always allow";
  - line 58: `UNATTENDED_SAFE_BUILTIN_TOOLS`;
  - lines 138–148: `toolRequiresApproval`.
- `packages/adapters/src/run-tool-request.ts`:
  - lines 91–95: arg validation before the effect is stored;
  - lines 157–243: approved replay, where `approvedReplayArgs` replaces the args with the stored request;
  - lines 290–340: `prepareToolRequest` sets `request.fleetSummary` and `request.effectRequest = args`. Fleet tools resolve server-side data here, and on an approved replay (`nextApprovedTool === name`) they skip this.
- `packages/adapters/src/approval-ask.ts`:
  - lines 24, 36–66: `FleetCardSummary = { title, lines }`; with `options.summary` the card text is `summary.title` and the detail is `summary.lines.join("\n")`;
  - explicit tools get Allow once / Deny only.
- `packages/adapters/src/run-tool-gate.ts`:
  - line 483: `card = { reviewReason, summary: request.fleetSummary, … }`;
  - lines 543–548: approve/execute flow;
  - lines 612–613: `call.finish`.
- `packages/adapters/src/approval-effect.ts`:
  - lines 337–344: `approvalPausedToolResult`;
  - line 360: `DENIED_ACTION_ERROR`.
- `packages/adapters/src/executor-readonly-approval.test.ts`:
  - lines ~433 and 778–840: test fixture for pause → approve → replay.
- `packages/adapters/src/run-tools-integrations.ts` (lines 12–23): handler pattern using `call.effectKey`.
- `apps/api/src/git-proxy.ts` and `apps/api/src/git-push-policy.ts`: where `extraPushChecks` runs.

## Patterns to follow

**Server-resolved card (like fleet tools):**
```ts
if (name === "code_request_push" && nextApprovedTool !== name) {
  const prepared = await prepareCodePushRequest(ctx, args); // reads git state on the computer
  if (!prepared.ok) return { error: prepared.error };
  args = prepared.canonical;            // { repository, branch, ref, newSha, botRepositoryId }
  request.fleetSummary = prepared.summary; // { title: "Push to GitLab?", lines: [...] }
}
...
if (name === "code_request_push") request.effectRequest = args;
```
The approval binds to the canonical args, including `newSha`, so the replay after approval uses exactly what the user saw.

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `packages/adapters/src/code-repo-tools.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT** `prepareCodePushRequest(ctx, args)`.
  1. Resolve the binding by `fullPath`. It must be a GitLab binding; otherwise return `{ ok: false, error: "code_request_push is only needed for GitLab repositories; push directly." }`.
  2. Validate the branch: if `branch` doesn't start with `refs/heads/`, use `refs/heads/${branch}`. `isBotBranchRef(ref, branchPrefix)` must hold; otherwise return an error naming the prefix.
  3. On the computer, inside the clone:
     - `git rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}` gives `newSha`. If the branch doesn't exist locally, return an error.
     - Pick the base: `git rev-parse --verify refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` if it exists, else `refs/remotes/origin/<defaultBranch>`.
     - `git log --format=%h %s -n 20 <base>..<newSha>` gives the commit subjects.
     - `git diff --shortstat <base>...<newSha>` gives the diff stat.
     - `git diff --name-only <base>...<newSha> -- .gitlab-ci.yml` flags a CI change.
     - Run `git fetch origin` first; ignore its failure.
  4. Build the summary: `title: "Push to GitLab?"`, and `lines`:
     - `<fullPath> · <branch without refs/heads/>`
     - `Commit <newSha.slice(0, 12)>`
     - the commit lines
     - the shortstat
     - `Changes .gitlab-ci.yml` if detected
  5. Redact everything with `ctx.secrets` and cap it at 40 lines.
  6. Canonical args: `{ repository: fullPath, branch, ref, newSha, botRepositoryId }`.
- **IMPLEMENT** the `codeRequestPushTool(ctx, call)` handler. It runs only after approval.
  1. Insert a row with `prisma.gitPushApproval.create({ data: { spaceId, userId, runId: ctx.runId, botRepositoryId, ref, newSha, effectId: call.effectKey } })`. Make it idempotent: on a unique violation of `effectId`, read the existing row.
  2. `return call.finish({ approved: true, branch, commit: newSha.slice(0, 12), next: "Run git push now; this approval covers exactly this commit." })`.
- Add `code_request_push` to `CODE_REPO_TOOL_NAMES`.
- Tool definition in `builtin-tools.ts`:
  - **description:** "Ask the user to approve pushing a branch of a GitLab repository. Every GitLab push needs one approval for the exact commit; commit first, call this, then git push. Not needed for GitHub."
  - **input:** `{ repository: string, branch: string }`, both required.
- Register the handler in `run-tools.ts`.
- **GOTCHA:** offer the tool only when the bot has at least one GitLab binding. Extend the executor's `codeReposEnabled` computation (in `executor.ts`, near the `selectBuiltinToolsForRun` call) with `gitlabPushApproval` (any binding whose `connection.provider === "gitlab"`). Drop `code_request_push` when it is false.

### UPDATE `packages/adapters/src/run-tool-request.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: the prepare branch shown in the pattern above, and `request.effectRequest = args` for `code_request_push`.
- **GOTCHA:** on approved replay, `prepare` must not run again. The stored canonical args include `newSha`.

### UPDATE `packages/core/src/action-approval.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: add `code_request_push` to `EXPLICIT_APPROVAL_BUILTIN_TOOLS`. It is never auto-approved and never "always allow". Don't add it to `UNATTENDED_SAFE_BUILTIN_TOOLS`. Update any exhaustive-list tests.

### CREATE `apps/api/src/git-push-approval.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT** `gitlabPushApprovalCheck(prisma): ExtraPushCheck`, a function of `{ run, binding, connection, commands }`.
  1. If `connection.provider !== "gitlab"`, return `{ ok: true }`.
  2. For each command, find an approval with `prisma.gitPushApproval.findFirst({ where: { runId: run.id, botRepositoryId: binding.id, ref, usedAt: null }, orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" } })`.
     - None found: `{ ok: false, message: "rakazo: GitLab pushes need approval; call code_request_push first" }`.
     - Found, but `newSha` differs: `{ ok: false, message: "rakazo: the approved commit was <sha7>; call code_request_push again" }`.
  3. Once every command matches, consume the approvals atomically with `prisma.gitPushApproval.updateMany({ where: { id: { in: ids }, usedAt: null }, data: { usedAt: new Date() } })`. If the count is smaller than `ids.length`, a concurrent push consumed one; refuse with the first message.
- Wire it into `mountGitProxyRoutes(app, { ..., extraPushChecks: [gitlabPushApprovalCheck(prisma)] })` in `apps/api/src/app.ts`.
- **GOTCHA:** this check runs after `checkPushCommands`/`checkFastForwards` and before forwarding. A consumed approval isn't restored if the host later rejects the push; the bot asks again. That keeps "exactly one push".

### Tests
- **`packages/adapters/src/code-request-push.test.ts`**, using the approval fixture from `executor-readonly-approval.test.ts`:
  1. The first call pauses with an ask block whose `text === "Push to GitLab?"`. Its detail contains the branch, a 12-char SHA and the commit subjects. Its actions are only `allow`/`deny`.
  2. After the effect is set to `approved`, the run continues, the handler inserts exactly one `GitPushApproval` with the stored `newSha`, and a repeated replay inserts no second row.
  3. A branch outside the prefix returns an error before any effect is recorded.
  4. A GitHub binding returns the "not needed" error.
  - Use a stub sandbox that answers the git commands.
- **`apps/api/src/git-push.integration.test.ts`**: extend the existing file, in the GitLab-only section with `describe.skipIf(!hasGit())`.
  1. A push without an approval is refused with `need approval`.
  2. Insert an approval for the local HEAD SHA, then push: it succeeds, and the approval now has `usedAt`.
  3. A second push of a new commit without a new approval is refused.
  4. An approval for a different SHA is refused with `the approved commit was`.
  5. GitHub pushes still succeed with no approval rows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `code_request_push` exists only for bots with a GitLab binding and a computer. It shows the explicit card "Push to GitLab?" with branch, commit SHA, commit subjects and diff stat, built from server-read data. The buttons are Allow once and Deny.
- [ ] Approval stores exactly one `GitPushApproval` bound to run, binding, ref and SHA. Approved replays are idempotent.
- [ ] A GitLab push is forwarded only when every ref update matches an unused approval from the same run. Approvals are consumed atomically, and one approval allows exactly one push.
- [ ] Refusals read as git errors: `remote: rakazo: GitLab pushes need approval; call code_request_push first`.
- [ ] GitHub pushes are unaffected.
- [ ] Tests pass: `pnpm vitest run packages/adapters/src/code-request-push.test.ts apps/api/src/git-push.integration.test.ts`

## Validation commands

```bash
pnpm lint && pnpm check
pnpm vitest run packages/adapters/src/code-request-push.test.ts apps/api/src/git-push.integration.test.ts packages/core/src
```
